To avoid transpose false positives: only consider a `'` as a string-open if the character BEFORE it is NOT a letter/digit/`)`/`]`/`}`/`.`/space-continuation (a transpose follows a value; a string-open follows an operator, `(`, `[`, `{`, `=`, `,`, `;`, `:` or line start).

50: x = A.';           % transpose
51: x = "multi

55: %}

# SYNTAX G2 — Unterminated Strings & Comments (3 checks) — Corrected Plan

**Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/syntax_errors.rs` — SyntaxErrorsEngine (file-level). Sub-checks gated by `is_check_enabled`.

## Checks
| ID | Message | Severity |
|----|---------|----------|
| STRIN | A quoted character vector is unterminated. | Error |
| DOUQT | A double quoted string is unterminated. | Error |
| INBLK | A block comment is unterminated at the end of the file. | Error |

## Detection
Triage (VERIFIED via astprobe — these are the actual parse shapes):
- `x = 'abc;` → `assignment "x = 'abc"` + ERROR `'`. A single-quoted char vector is terminated by the closing `'` OR end-of-line. An unmatched `'` before EOL is unterminated.
- `x = "abc;` → top-level `ERROR "x = \"abc;"`. Double-quoted strings can span newlines, so DOUQT only fires if there's no closing `"` before EOF.
- `%{\nunterminated` → parses as a single `comment` node whose text starts with `%{` and has no `%}`.

### STRIN — unterminated single-quoted char vector
Single quotes are tricky: `'` is also the **transpose** operator (`A'`, `A.'`) and the **complex conjugate transpose** (`A'`). A naive "odd count per line" scan will false-positive on `x = A';`.

**Robust approach — use the parse tree:** a char vector is a `string` node (kind `"string"`, with `string_content` child and `'` tokens). The unterminated case parses as `ERROR` containing a `'` (the astprobe showed `ERROR "'"`). Detection:
1. Walk ERROR nodes whose text starts with `'` (an unmatched opening quote).
2. ALSO handle the pattern where a `string` node's text ends with `'` but the closing `'` is missing (the probe showed `assignment "x = 'abc"` — the assignment consumed `'abc` as a string; the trailing `'` became ERROR).
3. Pragmatic: fire STRIN when an ERROR node contains a lone `'` at a position that is not a transpose (i.e., the ERROR text is exactly `'` or starts with `'` and the preceding token isn't a value/`)`/`]`/`}` that a transpose would follow).

**Simplest reliable rule:** a `'` is unterminated when it opens a char vector on a line and no matching `'` appears before end-of-line. To avoid transpose false positives: only consider a `'` as a string-open if the character BEFORE it is NOT a letter/digit/`)`/`]`/`}`/`.`/space-continuation (a transpose follows a value; a string-open follows an operator, `(`, `[`, `{`, `=`, `,`, `;`, `:` or line start).

### DOUQT — unterminated double-quoted string
Scan source (respecting comments via existing `collect_skip_ranges`): find a `"` that opens a string (preceding char is an operator/`(`/`,`/space/etc.) with no matching `"` before EOF. Double-quoted strings span newlines, so only EOF matters. Fire DOUQT at the opening `"`.

### INBLK — unterminated block comment
Walk the tree for `comment` nodes. If a comment node's text starts with `%{` and does NOT contain `%}`, fire INBLK.

Add `check_unterminated(root, source)` called from `check_file` (a new step after `check_error_nodes`).

## MUST fire
```matlab
x = 'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched ' before EOL
x = "abc;          % DOUQT: no closing " before EOF
%{
unterminated       % INBLK: no %}
```

## MUST NOT fire
```matlab
x = 'abc';         % closed char vector
x = "abc";         % closed string
x = 'it''s ok';    % escaped quote
x = A';            % transpose — NOT a string
x = A.';           % transpose
x = "multi
line";             % double-quoted string spans lines (valid)
%{
closed
%}
```

## Files
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/syntax_errors.rs` — `check_unterminated` + dispatch, module doc rows, tests.
- `docs/strin.md`, `docs/douqt.md`, `docs/inblk.md` (new).
- `docs/rules.md` — rows.
- `zensical.toml` — nav entries.

## Tests
- fires/not-fires per check (include the transpose not-fire cases for STRIN).
- config disabled suppresses.

## Pitfalls
- STRIN must NOT fire on `A'` transpose (preceding-char check).
- `''` (doubled quote) is an escaped quote inside char vectors.
- Double-quoted strings can span lines; DOUQT only fires if unclosed at EOF.
- Block comment: `%{` opens, `%}` closes; a comment node starting with `%{` without `%}` is INBLK.
- Verify the ERROR-node shape for `x = 'abc;` before relying on the string-node approach; adapt to what the parser actually produces.

1: //! # Syntax Errors: Parser-Level and Semantic Syntax Validation
2: //!
3: //! This module implements syntax error checks that detect issues tree-sitter flags
4: //! as ERROR/MISSING nodes, as well as semantic syntax issues the parser cannot catch
5: //! (invalid operators, bad file names, structural violations).
6: //!
7: //! ## Check IDs
8: //!
9: //! | Check ID | Description                                              |
10: //! |----------|----------------------------------------------------------|
11: //! | SYNER    | ERROR node detected in parse tree                        |
12: //! | BDFIL    | File name doesn't follow MATLAB naming rules             |
13: //! | BADNE    | Source contains `!=` (MATLAB uses `~=`)                  |
14: //! | BADOT    | Source contains `..` not part of `...`                   |
15: //! | TWOCM    | Source contains `,,`                                     |
16: //! | CLIS     | class_definition in a script file                        |
17: //! | CLTWO    | Multiple class_definition nodes in one file              |
18: //! | SOFOC    | Statements outside a class_definition in a class file    |
19: //! | SEMFU    | File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace) |
20: //! | FNDOT    | Function name contains dots outside class methods block  |
21: //! | FNSWA    | Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character    |
22: //! | NOPAR    | ERROR node looks like a missing closing bracket          |
23: //! | ENDCT    | ERROR node suggesting missing END                        |
24: //! | EOFMI    | File ends with ERROR node (incomplete)                   |
25: //! | NOLHS    | Assignment with empty left side                          |
26: //! | BADCH    | Invalid control characters in source                     |
27: //! | BADSP    | Non-ASCII whitespace characters in source                |
28: //! | REDEF    | Same identifier used as both function name and variable  |
29: //! | SEPEXR   | Missing newline/semicolon between statements             |
30: //!
31: //! ## Configuration
32: //!
33: //! ```toml
34: //! [lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]
35: //! disabled_checks = []
36: //! ```
37: 
38: use std::collections::HashSet;
39: use std::ops::Range;
40: 
41: use mlt_core::{Category, Config, Diagnostic, FileContext, Rule, Severity};
42: use serde::Deserialize;
43: use tree_sitter::Node;
44: 
45: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
46: // Rule-specific configuration
47: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48: 
49: /// Configuration for syntax error checks.
50: ///
51: /// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
52: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
53: pub struct SyntaxErrorsConfig {
54:     /// List of individual check IDs to disable (e.g., `["BADOT", "TWOCM"]`).
55:     #[serde(default)]
56:     pub disabled_checks: Vec<String>,
57: }
58: 
59: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
60: // Rule implementation
61: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
62: 
63: /// Syntax Errors Engine: a file-level rule that performs parser-level and
64: /// semantic syntax validation in a single pass.
65: pub struct SyntaxErrorsEngine {
66:     /// Set of disabled check IDs for fast lookup.
67:     disabled: HashSet<String>,
68: }
69: 
70: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
71:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
72:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
73:         let rule_config: SyntaxErrorsConfig = config.rule_params("SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE");
74:         let disabled: HashSet<String> = rule_config.disabled_checks.into_iter().collect();
75:         Box::new(Self { disabled })
76:     }
77: 
78:     /// Returns true if the given check ID is enabled.
79:     fn is_check_enabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
80:         !self.disabled.contains(check_id)
81:     }
82: 
83:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
84:     // Source text scanning (BADNE, BADOT, TWOCM, BADCH, BADSP)
85:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
86: 
87:     /// Collect byte ranges of all comment and string nodes to skip during
88:     /// source-level scanning.
89:     fn collect_skip_ranges(node: Node, ranges: &mut Vec<Range<usize>>) {
90:         if node.kind() == "comment" || node.kind() == "string" {
91:             ranges.push(node.byte_range());
92:             return;
93:         }
94:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
95:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
96:             Self::collect_skip_ranges(child, ranges);
97:         }
98:     }
99: 
100:     /// Check if a byte position is inside a skip range.
101:     fn in_skip_range(pos: usize, ranges: &[Range<usize>]) -> bool {
102:         ranges.iter().any(|r| r.contains(&pos))
103:     }
104: 
105:     /// Scan source text for BADNE (`!=`), BADOT (`..` not `...`), TWOCM (`,,`),
106:     /// BADCH (invalid control chars), and BADSP (non-ASCII whitespace).
107:     fn scan_source_text(
108:         &self,
109:         source: &str,
110:         skip_ranges: &[Range<usize>],
111:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
112:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
113:         let bytes = source.as_bytes();
114:         let len = bytes.len();
115: 
116:         // Track line/column for diagnostics.
117:         let mut line = 1usize;
118:         let mut line_start = 0usize;
119: 
120:         let mut i = 0;
121:         while i < len {
122:             let b = bytes[i];
123: 
124:             // Track newlines.
125:             if b == b'\n' {
126:                 line += 1;
127:                 line_start = i + 1;
128:                 i += 1;
129:                 continue;
130:             }
131: 
132:             // BADCH: Invalid control characters (< 0x20 except \t, \n, \r).
133:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADCH")
134:                 && b < 0x20
135:                 && b != b'\t'
136:                 && b != b'\n'
137:                 && b != b'\r'
138:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
139:             {
140:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
141:                     rule_id: "BADCH",
142:                     message: format!(
143:                         "Invalid control character (0x{:02X}) in source",
144:                         b
145:                     ),
146:                     severity: Severity::Error,
147:                     byte_range: i..i + 1,
148:                     line,
149:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
150:                     fix: None,
151:                 });
152:                 i += 1;
153:                 continue;
154:             }
155: 
156:             // BADSP: Non-ASCII whitespace detection.
157:             // Check for multi-byte UTF-8 sequences that are whitespace.
158:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADSP") && b > 0x7F && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges) {
159:                 // Decode the UTF-8 character at this position.
160:                 if let Some(ch) = source[i..].chars().next() {
161:                     if ch.is_whitespace() && ch != ' ' && ch != '\t' && ch != '\n' && ch != '\r' {
162:                         let ch_len = ch.len_utf8();
163:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
164:                             rule_id: "BADSP",
165:                             message: format!(
166:                                 "Non-ASCII whitespace character (U+{:04X}) in source",
167:                                 ch as u32
168:                             ),
169:                             severity: Severity::Error,
170:                             byte_range: i..i + ch_len,
171:                             line,
172:                             column: i - line_start + 1,
173:                             fix: None,
174:                         });
175:                         i += ch_len;
176:                         continue;
177:                     }
178:                 }
179:             }
180: 
181:             // BADNE: `!=` (MATLAB uses `~=`).
182:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADNE")
183:                 && b == b'!'
184:                 && i + 1 < len
185:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b'='
186:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
187:             {
188:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
189:                     rule_id: "BADNE",
190:                     message: "Use '~=' instead of '!=' for not-equal in MATLAB".to_string(),
191:                     severity: Severity::Error,
192:                     byte_range: i..i + 2,
193:                     line,
194:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
195:                     fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::new(i..i + 2, "~=")),
196:                 });
197:                 i += 2;
198:                 continue;
199:             }
200: 
201:             // BADOT: `..` not part of `...` (line continuation).
202:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADOT")
203:                 && b == b'.'
204:                 && i + 1 < len
205:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b'.'
206:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
207:             {
208:                 // Check if this is part of `...` (line continuation).
209:                 let is_ellipsis = i + 2 < len && bytes[i + 2] == b'.';
210:                 if !is_ellipsis {
211:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
212:                         rule_id: "BADOT",
213:                         message: "Invalid '..' operator; did you mean '...' (line continuation)?"
214:                             .to_string(),
215:                         severity: Severity::Error,
216:                         byte_range: i..i + 2,
217:                         line,
218:                         column: i - line_start + 1,
219:                         fix: None,
220:                     });
221:                     i += 2;
222:                     continue;
223:                 } else {
224:                     // Skip the whole `...`.
225:                     i += 3;
226:                     continue;
227:                 }
228:             }
229: 
230:             // TWOCM: `,,` (double comma).
231:             if self.is_check_enabled("TWOCM")
232:                 && b == b','
233:                 && i + 1 < len
234:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b','
235:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
236:             {
237:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
238:                     rule_id: "TWOCM",
239:                     message: "Double comma ',,'; possible typo".to_string(),
240:                     severity: Severity::Error,
241:                     byte_range: i..i + 2,
242:                     line,
243:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
244:                     fix: None,
245:                 });
246:                 i += 2;
247:                 continue;
248:             }
249: 
250:             // Advance past multi-byte UTF-8 characters.
251:             if b > 0x7F {
252:                 if let Some(ch) = source[i..].chars().next() {
253:                     i += ch.len_utf8();
254:                     continue;
255:                 }
256:             }
257: 
258:             i += 1;
259:         }
260: 
261:         diagnostics
262:     }
263: 
264:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
265:     // Tree ERROR/MISSING node analysis (SYNER, NOPAR, ENDCT, EOFMI)
266:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
267: 
268:     /// Walk the tree and collect diagnostics for ERROR and MISSING nodes.
269:     fn check_error_nodes(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
270:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
271:         self.walk_error_nodes(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
272: 
273:         // EOFMI: Check if file ends with ERROR node.
274:         if self.is_check_enabled("EOFMI") {
275:             if let Some(last) = Self::last_descendant(root) {
276:                 if last.is_error() || last.is_missing() {
277:                     let start = last.start_byte();
278:                     let end = last.end_byte().max(start + 1);
279:                     let pos = last.start_position();
280:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
281:                         rule_id: "EOFMI",
282:                         message: "File ends with an incomplete or erroneous construct"
283:                             .to_string(),
284:                         severity: Severity::Error,
285:                         byte_range: start..end,
286:                         line: pos.row + 1,
287:                         column: pos.column + 1,
288:                         fix: None,
289:                     });
290:                 }
291:             }
292:         }
293: 
294:         diagnostics
295:     }
296: 
297:     /// Recursive DFS to find ERROR/MISSING nodes and classify them.
298:     fn walk_error_nodes(
299:         &self,
300:         node: Node,
301:         source: &str,
302:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
303:     ) {
304:         if node.is_error() {
305:             let start = node.start_byte();
306:             let end = node.end_byte().max(start + 1);
307:             let pos = node.start_position();
308:             let text = &source[start..end.min(source.len())];
309: 
310:             // Classify the error node.
311:             // NOPAR: Looks like a missing closing bracket.
312:             if self.is_check_enabled("NOPAR") && Self::looks_like_missing_bracket(text) {
313:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
314:                     rule_id: "NOPAR",
315:                     message: "Possible missing closing bracket/parenthesis".to_string(),
316:                     severity: Severity::Error,
317:                     byte_range: start..end,
318:                     line: pos.row + 1,
319:                     column: pos.column + 1,
320:                     fix: None,
321:                 });
322:             }
323:             // ENDCT: Looks like a missing END.
324:             else if self.is_check_enabled("ENDCT") && Self::looks_like_missing_end(text, &node) {
325:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
326:                     rule_id: "ENDCT",
327:                     message: "Possible missing 'end' keyword".to_string(),
328:                     severity: Severity::Error,
329:                     byte_range: start..end,
330:                     line: pos.row + 1,
331:                     column: pos.column + 1,
332:                     fix: None,
333:                 });
334:             }
335:             // SYNER: Generic syntax error.
336:             else if self.is_check_enabled("SYNER") {
337:                 let snippet: String = text.chars().take(40).collect();
338:                 let msg = if snippet.is_empty() {
339:                     "Syntax error".to_string()
340:                 } else {
341:                     format!("Syntax error near '{snippet}'")
342:                 };
343:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
344:                     rule_id: "SYNER",
345:                     message: msg,
346:                     severity: Severity::Error,
347:                     byte_range: start..end,
348:                     line: pos.row + 1,
349:                     column: pos.column + 1,
350:                     fix: None,
351:                 });
352:             }
353:         } else if node.is_missing() && self.is_check_enabled("SYNER") {
354:             let start = node.start_byte();
355:             let end = node.end_byte().max(start + 1);
356:             let pos = node.start_position();
357:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
358:                 rule_id: "SYNER",
359:                 message: format!("Missing expected '{}'", node.kind()),
360:                 severity: Severity::Error,
361:                 byte_range: start..end,
362:                 line: pos.row + 1,
363:                 column: pos.column + 1,
364:                 fix: None,
365:             });
366:         }
367: 
368:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
369:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
370:             self.walk_error_nodes(child, source, diagnostics);
371:         }
372:     }
373: 
374:     /// Heuristic: does this error text look like an unclosed bracket?
375:     fn looks_like_missing_bracket(text: &str) -> bool {
376:         let opens: usize = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == '(' || c == '[' || c == '{').count();
377:         let closes: usize = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == ')' || c == ']' || c == '}').count();
378:         opens > closes
379:     }
380: 
381:     /// Heuristic: does this error look like a missing `end`?
382:     fn looks_like_missing_end(text: &str, node: &Node) -> bool {
383:         // If the error node is preceded by block-opening keywords.
384:         let block_openers = [
385:             "if", "for", "while", "switch", "try", "function", "classdef",
386:             "properties", "methods", "events", "enumeration",
387:         ];
388:         // Check text for block openers without matching end.
389:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
390:         let has_opener = block_openers.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
391:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
392: 
393:         if has_opener && !has_end {
394:             return true;
395:         }
396: 
397:         // Check if previous sibling is a block statement.
398:         if let Some(prev) = node.prev_sibling() {
399:             let kind = prev.kind();
400:             if block_openers.contains(&kind) {
401:                 return true;
402:             }
403:         }
404: 
405:         false
406:     }

408:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
409:     // File structure validation (BDFIL, CLIS, CLTWO, SOFOC, SEMFU)
410:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
411: 
412:     /// Validate file name against MATLAB naming rules.
413:     fn check_file_name(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
414:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
415: 
416:         if !self.is_check_enabled("BDFIL") {
417:             return diagnostics;
418:         }
419: 
420:         if let Some(stem) = ctx.file_path.file_stem() {
421:             let name = stem.to_string_lossy();
422: 
423:             let valid = !name.is_empty()
424:                 && name.len() <= 63
425:                 && name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
426:                 && name.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_');
427: 
428:             if !valid {
429:                 let reason = if name.is_empty() {
430:                     "file name is empty".to_string()
431:                 } else if name.len() > 63 {
432:                     format!("file name exceeds 63 characters ({} chars)", name.len())
433:                 } else if !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()) {
434:                     "file name must start with a letter".to_string()
435:                 } else {
436:                     "file name contains invalid characters (only alphanumeric and underscore allowed)".to_string()
437:                 };
438:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
439:                     rule_id: "BDFIL",
440:                     message: format!("Invalid MATLAB file name '{}': {}", name, reason),
441:                     severity: Severity::Error,
442:                     byte_range: 0..ctx.source.len().min(1),
443:                     line: 1,
444:                     column: 1,
445:                     fix: None,
446:                 });
447:             }
448:         }
449: 
450:         diagnostics
451:     }
452: 
453:     /// Check for class/script structure issues (CLIS, CLTWO, SOFOC, SEMFU).
454:     fn check_file_structure(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
455:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
456:         let mut cursor = root.walk();
457: 
458:         let mut class_count = 0usize;
459:         let mut has_non_class_statements = false;
460:         let mut has_function_def = false;
461:         let mut has_any_real_content = false;
462: 
463:         for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
464:             let kind = child.kind();
465:             match kind {
466:                 "class_definition" => class_count += 1,
467:                 "function_definition" => {
468:                     has_function_def = true;
469:                     has_any_real_content = true;
470:                 }
471:                 "comment" => {} // Comments don't count as content.
472:                 "expression_statement" => {
473:                     // Check if it's just a semicolon.
474:                     let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
475:                     let trimmed = text.trim();
476:                     if trimmed == ";" {
477:                         // Empty statement — doesn't count as real content.
478:                     } else {
479:                         has_non_class_statements = true;
480:                         has_any_real_content = true;
481:                     }
482:                 }
483:                 _ if !child.is_error() && kind != "\n" => {
484:                     has_non_class_statements = true;
485:                     has_any_real_content = true;
486:                 }
487:                 _ => {}
488:             }
489:         }
490: 
491:         // CLTWO: Multiple class definitions in one file.
492:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLTWO") && class_count > 1 {
493:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
494:                 rule_id: "CLTWO",
495:                 message: format!(
496:                     "File contains {class_count} class definitions; only one is allowed per file"
497:                 ),
498:                 severity: Severity::Error,
499:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
500:                 line: 1,
501:                 column: 1,
502:                 fix: None,
503:             });
504:         }
505: 
506:         // CLIS: Class definition in a script file (non-function statements exist).
507:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLIS")
508:             && class_count > 0
509:             && has_non_class_statements
510:             && !has_function_def
511:         {
512:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
513:                 rule_id: "CLIS",
514:                 message: "Class definition in a script file; statements exist outside the class"
515:                     .to_string(),
516:                 severity: Severity::Error,
517:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
518:                 line: 1,
519:                 column: 1,
520:                 fix: None,
521:             });
522:         }
523: 
524:         // SOFOC: Statements outside a class definition in a class file.
525:         if self.is_check_enabled("SOFOC")
526:             && class_count > 0
527:             && has_non_class_statements
528:             && has_function_def
529:         {
530:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
531:                 rule_id: "SOFOC",
532:                 message:
533:                     "Statements outside class definition in a class file are not allowed"
534:                         .to_string(),
535:                 severity: Severity::Error,
536:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
537:                 line: 1,
538:                 column: 1,
539:                 fix: None,
540:             });
541:         }
542: 
543:         // SEMFU: File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace).
544:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEMFU")
545:             && !has_any_real_content
546:             && class_count == 0
547:             && !source.trim().is_empty()
548:         {
549:             // Verify the file truly only has semicolons, whitespace, and comments.
550:             let only_empty = source
551:                 .lines()
552:                 .all(|line| {
553:                     let trimmed = line.trim();
554:                     trimmed.is_empty()
555:                         || trimmed == ";"
556:                         || trimmed.starts_with('%')
557:                 });
558:             if only_empty {
559:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
560:                     rule_id: "SEMFU",
561:                     message: "File contains only empty statements (semicolons and whitespace)"
562:                         .to_string(),
563:                     severity: Severity::Error,
564:                     byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
565:                     line: 1,
566:                     column: 1,
567:                     fix: None,
568:                 });
569:             }
570:         }
571: 
572:         diagnostics
573:     }

575:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
576:     // Function name validation (FNDOT, FNSWA)
577:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
578: 
579:     /// Check function names for issues (FNDOT, FNSWA).
580:     fn check_function_names(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
581:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
582:         self.walk_function_names(root, source, &mut diagnostics, false);
583:         diagnostics
584:     }
585: 
586:     /// Recursively walk to find function_definition nodes and validate names.
587:     fn walk_function_names(
588:         &self,
589:         node: Node,
590:         source: &str,
591:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
592:         in_methods_block: bool,
593:     ) {
594:         let kind = node.kind();
595:         let is_methods = kind == "methods";
596: 
597:         if kind == "function_definition" {
598:             // Find the function name node.
599:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
600:                 let name = &source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()];
601:                 let pos = name_node.start_position();
602: 
603:                 // FNSWA: Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character.
604:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNSWA")
605:                     && !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
606:                 {
607:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
608:                         rule_id: "FNSWA",
609:                         message: format!(
610:                             "Function name '{}' must start with an alphabetic character",
611:                             name
612:                         ),
613:                         severity: Severity::Error,
614:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
615:                         line: pos.row + 1,
616:                         column: pos.column + 1,
617:                         fix: None,
618:                     });
619:                 }
620: 
621:                 // FNDOT: Function name contains dots but is not in a class methods block.
622:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNDOT") && name.contains('.') && !in_methods_block {
623:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
624:                         rule_id: "FNDOT",
625:                         message: format!(
626:                             "Function name '{}' contains dots but is not in a class methods block",
627:                             name
628:                         ),
629:                         severity: Severity::Error,
630:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
631:                         line: pos.row + 1,
632:                         column: pos.column + 1,
633:                         fix: None,
634:                     });
635:                 }
636:             }
637:         }
638: 
639:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
640:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
641:             self.walk_function_names(
642:                 child,
643:                 source,
644:                 diagnostics,
645:                 in_methods_block || is_methods,
646:             );
647:         }
648:     }
649: 
650:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
651:     // Statement validation (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF)
652:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
653: 
654:     /// Check statements for issues (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF).
655:     fn check_statements(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
656:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
657: 
658:         // Collect function names and variable assignments for REDEF.
659:         let mut function_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
660:         let mut variable_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
661:         let mut redef_reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
662: 
663:         self.walk_statements(
664:             root,
665:             source,
666:             &mut diagnostics,
667:             &mut function_names,
668:             &mut variable_names,
669:             &mut redef_reported,
670:         );
671: 
672:         diagnostics
673:     }
674: 
675:     /// Recursively walk statements for validation.
676:     fn walk_statements(
677:         &self,
678:         node: Node,
679:         source: &str,
680:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
681:         function_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
682:         variable_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
683:         redef_reported: &mut HashSet<String>,
684:     ) {
685:         let kind = node.kind();
686: 
687:         // NOLHS: Assignment with empty left side.
688:         if self.is_check_enabled("NOLHS") && kind == "assignment" {
689:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
690:                 let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
691:                 if lhs_text.trim().is_empty() {
692:                     let pos = node.start_position();
693:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
694:                         rule_id: "NOLHS",
695:                         message: "Assignment with empty left-hand side".to_string(),
696:                         severity: Severity::Error,
697:                         byte_range: node.byte_range(),
698:                         line: pos.row + 1,
699:                         column: pos.column + 1,
700:                         fix: None,
701:                     });
702:                 }
703:             }
704:         }
705: 
706:         // REDEF: Track function definitions and variable assignments.
707:         if kind == "function_definition" {
708:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
709:                 let name = source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()].to_string();
710:                 if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
711:                     && variable_names.contains(&name)
712:                     && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
713:                 {
714:                     let pos = name_node.start_position();
715:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
716:                         rule_id: "REDEF",
717:                         message: format!(
718:                             "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
719:                             name
720:                         ),
721:                         severity: Severity::Error,
722:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
723:                         line: pos.row + 1,
724:                         column: pos.column + 1,
725:                         fix: None,
726:                     });
727:                     redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
728:                 }
729:                 function_names.insert(name);
730:             }
731:         }
732: 
733:         if kind == "assignment" {
734:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
735:                 let lhs_kind = lhs.kind();
736:                 if lhs_kind == "identifier" {
737:                     let name = source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()].to_string();
738:                     if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
739:                         && function_names.contains(&name)
740:                         && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
741:                     {
742:                         let pos = lhs.start_position();
743:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
744:                             rule_id: "REDEF",
745:                             message: format!(
746:                                 "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
747:                                 name
748:                             ),
749:                             severity: Severity::Error,
750:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
751:                             line: pos.row + 1,
752:                             column: pos.column + 1,
753:                             fix: None,
754:                         });
755:                         redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
756:                     }
757:                     variable_names.insert(name);
758:                 }
759:             }
760:         }
761: 
762:         // SEPEXR: Missing separator between statements.
763:         // Check consecutive children of block/source_file that are statements
764:         // on the same line without separator.
765:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEPEXR") && (kind == "source_file" || kind == "block") {
766:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
767:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
768: 
769:             for pair in children.windows(2) {
770:                 let prev = pair[0];
771:                 let curr = pair[1];
772: 
773:                 // Skip error nodes and comments.
774:                 if prev.is_error() || curr.is_error() {
775:                     continue;
776:                 }
777:                 if prev.kind() == "comment" || curr.kind() == "comment" {
778:                     continue;
779:                 }
780: 
781:                 // Check if they're on the same line with no separator.
782:                 let prev_end = prev.end_position();
783:                 let curr_start = curr.start_position();
784: 
785:                 if prev_end.row == curr_start.row {
786:                     // Check the text between them for a separator (; or ,).
787:                     let between_start = prev.end_byte();
788:                     let between_end = curr.start_byte();
789:                     if between_start < between_end {
790:                         let between = &source[between_start..between_end];
791:                         let has_separator =
792:                             between.contains(';') || between.contains(',');
793:                         if !has_separator {
794:                             let pos = curr.start_position();
795:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
796:                                 rule_id: "SEPEXR",
797:                                 message:
798:                                     "Missing semicolon or newline between statements"
799:                                         .to_string(),
800:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
801:                                 byte_range: curr.byte_range(),
802:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
803:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
804:                                 fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::insert(between_start, ";")),
805:                             });
806:                         }
807:                     }
808:                 }
809:             }
810:         }
811: 
812:         // Recurse into children.
813:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
814:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
815:             self.walk_statements(
816:                 child,
817:                 source,
818:                 diagnostics,
819:                 function_names,
820:                 variable_names,
821:                 redef_reported,
822:             );
823:         }
824:     }

826:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
827:     // Helpers
828:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
829: 
830:     /// Find the last (rightmost, deepest) descendant node in a tree.
831:     fn last_descendant(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
832:         let child_count = node.child_count();
833:         if child_count == 0 {
834:             return Some(node);
835:         }
836:         let last_child = node.child(child_count - 1)?;
837:         Self::last_descendant(last_child)
838:     }
839: }

841: impl Rule for SyntaxErrorsEngine {
842:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
843:         "SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE"
844:     }
845: 
846:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
847:         "Parser-level and semantic syntax validation"
848:     }
849: 
850:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
851:         Severity::Error
852:     }
853: 
854:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
855:         Category::SyntaxErrors
856:     }
857: 
858:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
859:         // File-level only — no node subscriptions.
860:         &[]
861:     }
862: 
863:     fn can_be_disabled(&self) -> bool {
864:         true
865:     }
866: 
867:     fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
868:         true
869:     }
870: 
871:     fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
872:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
873:         let root = ctx.tree.root_node();
874:         let source = ctx.source;
875: 
876:         // 1. File name validation (BDFIL).
877:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_file_name(ctx));
878: 
879:         // 2. Collect skip ranges (comments and strings) for source scanning.
880:         let mut skip_ranges = Vec::new();
881:         Self::collect_skip_ranges(root, &mut skip_ranges);
882: 
883:         // 3. Source text scanning (BADNE, BADOT, TWOCM, BADCH, BADSP).
884:         diagnostics.extend(self.scan_source_text(source, &skip_ranges));
885: 
886:         // 4. Tree ERROR/MISSING node analysis (SYNER, NOPAR, ENDCT, EOFMI).
887:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_error_nodes(root, source));
888: 
889:         // 5. File structure validation (CLIS, CLTWO, SOFOC, SEMFU).
890:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_file_structure(root, source));
891: 
892:         // 6. Function name validation (FNDOT, FNSWA).
893:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_function_names(root, source));
894: 
895:         // 7. Statement validation (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF).
896:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_statements(root, source));
897: 
898:         diagnostics
899:     }
900: }

# NOSEMI - Trailing Semicolon Missing

**Default severity:** Info
**Auto-fix:** Yes
**Category:** Formatting
**Can be disabled:** Yes

## What this rule does

Flags MATLAB statements that do not end with a trailing semicolon (`;`). This applies to statements that produce a value — primarily assignments, function calls, and commands at the statement level.

## Why this matters

- **Performance**: In loops, unsuppressed output causes significant slowdowns due to console I/O on every iteration
- **Noise**: Unintended console output clutters the Command Window, making it harder to find real output
- **Intent**: Without a semicolon, it's ambiguous whether the output was intentional (for debugging) or accidental
- **CI/CD**: Stray output in automated MATLAB scripts can pollute logs or interfere with output parsing

## Examples

display.text:
# NOSEMI - Trailing Semicolon Missing

**Default severity:** Info
**Auto-fix:** Yes
**Category:** Formatting
**Can be disabled:** Yes

## What this rule does

Flags MATLAB statements that do not end with a trailing semicolon (`;`). This applies to statements that produce a value — primarily assignments, function calls, and commands at the statement level.

## Why this matters

- **Performance**: In loops, unsuppressed output causes significant slowdowns due to console I/O on every iteration
- **Noise**: Unintended console output clutters the Command Window, making it harder to find real output
- **Intent**: Without a semicolon, it's ambiguous whether the output was intentional (for debugging) or accidental
- **CI/CD**: Stray output in automated MATLAB scripts can pollute logs or interfere with output parsing

## Examples

### Correct

```matlab
x = compute_value();
data = load('file.mat');
result = process(data);

% Intentional output (configure ignore_functions)
disp('Processing complete');
fprintf('Result: %d\n', result);
```

### Incorrect

```matlab
x = compute_value()
data = load('file.mat')
result = process(data)
```

### Fixed

```matlab
x = compute_value();
data = load('file.mat');
result = process(data);
```

## Configuration

```toml title=".mlt.toml"
[lint.rules.NOSEMI]
severity = "info"
ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf", "warning", "error"]
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `severity` | string | `"info"` | Severity level (`"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`, `"off"`) |
| `ignore_functions` | array of strings | `[]` | Function names to exclude from this check |

### `ignore_functions`

A list of function names that are commonly used for intentional console output. When a `function_call` or `command` statement calls one of these functions, the rule will not flag it even without a semicolon.

Common values:

```toml
ignore_functions = [
    "disp",
    "fprintf",
    "warning",
    "error",
    "assert",
    "sprintf",  # usually assigned, but sometimes standalone
]
```

## Automatic fixes

This rule inserts a semicolon (`;`) immediately after the end of the statement:

```diff
- x = compute_value()
+ x = compute_value();
```

The fix is always safe — it suppresses output but does not change program behavior.

## Target node types

This rule triggers on the following tree-sitter node types when they appear at statement level (direct children of `source_file` or `block`):

- `assignment` — Variable assignments (`a = expr`)
- `function_call` — Function calls used as statements (`foo(x)`)
- `command` — Command-syntax calls (`cd dir`, `help topic`)

Sub-expressions (e.g., `bar(1)` inside `x = foo(bar(1))`) are **not** flagged.

## Related rules

- `NOCOMMA` — Missing comma between matrix elements
- `NO4LP` — Missing indentation for loop body

# Rules Reference

## Overview

mlt implements lint rules matching MATLAB's Code Analyzer checks for feature parity. Rules use the same check IDs as MATLAB (e.g., `NOSEMI`, `AGROW`, `naming.class.casing`) and are organized into categories.

## Rule Table

| Rule ID | Category | Description | Default Severity | Auto-fix |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ---------------- | -------- |
| [NOSEMI](nosemi.md) | Formatting | Statement without trailing semicolon may produce unintended console output | Info | Yes |
| [MFAMB](mfamb.md) | Readability | Cannot determine whether name is a variable or function; assumes function | Info | No |
| [FLUDLR](fludlr.md) | Readability | Nested `flipud(fliplr(x))`/`fliplr(flipud(x))` should use `rot90(x, 2)` | Info | Yes |
| [STLOW](stlow.md) | Readability | Unnecessary UPPER/LOWER call in a comparison | Info | Yes |
| [COMNL](comnl.md) | Readability | Newline following comma acts as a row separator in a matrix; suggest semicolon or ellipsis | Info | Yes |
| [FVINR](fvinr.md) | Readability | For readability, add Input attribute to the input arguments block | Info | Yes |
| [NOFIL](nofil.md) | Incomplete Analysis | File not found | Error | No |
| [RDERR](rderr.md) | Incomplete Analysis | Unable to read file | Error | No |
| [QUIT](quit.md) | Incomplete Analysis | Code analysis did not complete; the analyzer encountered an internal error | Error | No |

## Rule Categories

mlt organizes rules into the same categories as MATLAB's Code Analyzer:

| Category | Config Key | Description |
| -------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| Incomplete Analysis | `incomplete-analysis` | Internal linter limits and analysis failures |
| Syntax Errors | `syntax-errors` | Parser-level syntax validation |
| Language Specification | `language-specification` | Language constraint violations |
| Bugs | `bugs` | Likely bugs and logic errors |
| Custom Checks | `custom-checks` | Configurable code complexity/style metrics |
| Naming | `naming` | Naming convention enforcement |
| Compatibility | `compatibility` | Deprecated/removed functions and APIs |
| Forward Compatibility | `forward-compatibility` | Forward compatibility issues |
| Good Practices | `good-practices` | Common best practices |
| Unset Variables | `unset-variables` | Variables that may not be defined before use |
| Unused Constructions | `unused-constructions` | Dead code and unused constructions |
| Suggested Improvements | `suggested-improvements` | Suggestions for improved code patterns |
| Readability | `readability` | Readability improvements |
| Formatting | `formatting` | Code formatting suggestions |
| Performance | `performance` | Performance improvement suggestions |
| Code Generation | `code-generation` | MATLAB Coder constraints |
| Fixed-Point | `fixed-point` | Fixed-point toolbox specific |
| Deployment | `deployment` | MATLAB Compiler deployment constraints |
| System Objects | `system-objects` | System object validation |
| Unsupported | `unsupported` | Unsupported features |
| Behavior Changes | `behavior-changes` | Behavior changes between MATLAB versions |
| Configuration Issues | `configuration-issues` | Configuration file validation |

## Severity Levels

Rules are categorized into three severity levels:

### Error

Critical issues that likely indicate bugs or broken code:

- Code that will fail at runtime
- Language specification violations
- Syntax errors

### Warning

Issues that affect code quality:

- Common bug patterns
- Good practice violations
- Deprecated function usage

### Info

Low-priority suggestions:

- Formatting preferences
- Performance improvement hints
- Readability suggestions

### Configuring Severity

Override default severities in `.mlt.toml`:

```toml
[lint.rules]
NOSEMI = "error"    # Upgrade from info to error
```

Or in a full table:

```toml
[lint.rules.NOSEMI]
severity = "error"
ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf"]
```

### Category-Level Configuration

Enable, disable, or override severity for entire categories:

```toml
[lint.categories]
performance = "off"           # Disable all performance rules
compatibility = "warn"        # Override all compatibility rules to warning
formatting = "info"           # Set all formatting rules to info
```

Per-rule configuration always takes precedence over category-level settings.

See [Configuration](configuration.md) for full details.

## Enabling and Disabling Rules

All rules are enabled by default. Disable individual rules:

```toml
[lint.rules]
NOSEMI = "off"
```

Or disable entire categories:

```toml
[lint.categories]
behavior-changes = "off"
```

## Auto-fix Support

Rules marked with "Yes" in the Auto-fix column provide automatic fixes. Run mlt with `--fix` to apply them:

```bash
mlt --fix src/**/*.m
```

Fixes are applied atomically per file. Overlapping fixes are detected and the conflicting fix is skipped with a warning.

## Adding New Rules

mlt uses auto-registration via the `inventory` crate. To add a new rule:

1. Create a new module in `crates/mlt_rules/src/` (e.g., `agrow.rs`)
2. Implement the `Rule` trait with a `from_config` factory
3. Add `inventory::submit!(crate::RuleRegistration::new("AGROW", Agrow::from_config));` at the bottom
4. Add documentation in `docs/agrow.md`

No manual edits to `lib.rs` are needed beyond adding the `pub mod` declaration.

See the [repository](https://github.com/watermarkhu/mlt) for the full development guide.

1: //! Shared utilities for rule-module unit tests.
2: //!
3: //! These helpers mirror the `Linter` dispatch so tests can exercise both
4: //! node-level (`check`) and file-level (`check_file`) rules directly,
5: //! without going through the full CLI.
6: //!
7: //! This module is only compiled under `#[cfg(test)]`.
8: 
9: use mlt_core::{Diagnostic, FileContext, NodeContext, Rule};
10: use tree_sitter::{Node, Parser};
11: 
12: /// Parse MATLAB source and return the tree.
13: pub fn parse(source: &str) -> tree_sitter::Tree {
14:     let mut parser = Parser::new();
15:     parser
16:         .set_language(&tree_sitter_matlab::LANGUAGE.into())
17:         .expect("failed to load tree-sitter-matlab");
18:     parser.parse(source, None).expect("parse failed")
19: }
20: 
21: /// Build a `FileContext` with a fixed test file path.
22: pub fn file_ctx<'a>(tree: &'a tree_sitter::Tree, source: &'a str) -> FileContext<'a> {
23:     FileContext {
24:         tree,
25:         source,
26:         file_path: std::path::Path::new("test.m"),
27:     }
28: }
29: 
30: /// Run a rule's node-level `check()` over every node in the tree, mimicking
31: /// the Linter's depth-first dispatch. Returns all diagnostics.
32: pub fn lint_nodes(rule: &dyn Rule, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
33:     let tree = parse(source);
34:     let path = std::path::Path::new("test.m");
35:     let targets: Vec<&str> = rule.target_node_types().to_vec();
36:     let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
37: 
38:     fn walk(
39:         node: Node,
40:         source: &str,
41:         path: &std::path::Path,
42:         targets: &[&str],
43:         rule: &dyn Rule,
44:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
45:     ) {
46:         if targets.contains(&node.kind()) {
47:             let ctx = NodeContext {
48:                 node,
49:                 source,
50:                 file_path: path,
51:             };
52:             diagnostics.extend(rule.check(&ctx));
53:         }
54:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
55:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
56:             walk(child, source, path, targets, rule, diagnostics);
57:         }
58:     }
59: 
60:     walk(tree.root_node(), source, path, &targets, rule, &mut diagnostics);
61:     diagnostics
62: }
63: 
64: /// Run a rule's file-level `check_file()`. Returns all diagnostics.
65: pub fn lint_file(rule: &dyn Rule, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
66:     let tree = parse(source);
67:     let ctx = file_ctx(&tree, source);
68:     rule.check_file(&ctx)
69: }
70: 
71: /// Returns true if any diagnostic has the given rule ID.
72: pub fn has_id(diags: &[Diagnostic], id: &str) -> bool {
73:     diags.iter().any(|d| d.rule_id == id)
74: }

(End of file - total 74 lines)

Now I have a very clear picture. Let me analyze the shapes:

**STRIN cases (unterminated single-quoted char vector):**
1. `x = 'abc;` → `assignment` contains ERROR at [4..5] text `'` (which itself contains a child ERROR at [4..5] text `'`). ERROR node text starts with `'`.
2. `x = 'don''t stop` → top-level ERROR [0..16] text `x = 'don''t stop`, containing `'` [4..5] and `string_content` [5..16] text `don''t stop`. Interesting — here the ERROR node's TEXT starts with `x`, not `'`. The `'` is a separate child token! And the string_content does NOT start with `'` — the `'` is its own node. Hmm, this differs from my earlier assumption.
3. `'abc` at file start → ERROR [0..1] text `'` containing `'`.
4. `disp('abc` → outer ERROR [0..9] text `disp('abc` containing inner ERROR [5..6] text `'`.
5. `foo('a', 'b` → outer ERROR [0..12] text `foo('a', 'b` containing string [4..7] (valid) and ERROR [9..10] text `'`.
6. `x = ';` → ERROR [2..5] text `= '` containing inner ERROR [4..5] text `'`.

**Key insight:** In ALL unterminated single-quote cases, there's an ERROR node whose text starts with `'` OR an ERROR node containing a child ERROR whose text starts with `'` (the inner ERROR [4..5] in `x = ';` has text `'`, but the parent ERROR has text `= '` which does NOT start with `'`... wait, `= '` — hmm the parent's text starts with `=`).

So the detection for STRIN: walk ERROR nodes; if an ERROR node's text starts with `'` → fire at that position. That covers cases 1, 3, 4 (inner ERROR [5..6] text `'`), 5 (inner ERROR [9..10] text `'`).

Case 2 (`x = 'don''t stop`) and case 6 (`x = ';`) need special handling:
- Case 2: top-level ERROR [0..16] text `x = 'don''t stop`. The `'` is a direct child at [4..5]. There's a `string_content` child. Hmm — how do I know this is an unterminated SINGLE quote vs the double-quote case `x = "abc;`?

Compare:
- `x = 'don''t stop` → ERROR contains: `identifier`, `=`, `'` (char token), `string_content`.
- `x = "abc;` → ERROR contains: `identifier`, `=`, `"` (char token), `string_content`.

They're IDENTICAL shapes! The only difference is the quote character: `'` vs `"`. So:
- If the ERROR contains a `'` token child followed by string_content, and the ERROR's parent is NOT a `string` node → STRIN.
- If the ERROR contains a `"` token child followed by string_content → DOUQT.

Actually, more precisely: the opening delimiter token is a direct child of the ERROR node. So the rule:
- Walk ERROR nodes. For each ERROR node, examine its children (and itself):
  - If the ERROR's text starts with `'` → STRIN (unterminated char vector; the opening quote has no content parsed).
  - If the ERROR contains a direct child token `'` that is not a transpose (i.e., not following a value) → STRIN.
  - If the ERROR contains a direct child token `"` → DOUQT (unterminated double-quoted string).

Hmm wait, but for case 6 (`x = ';`): ERROR [2..5] text `= '`, children `=` and inner ERROR [4..5] text `'`. The inner ERROR starts with `'` → my first rule fires on the inner ERROR. ✓ (I walk all ERROR nodes, including nested ones.)

For case 2 (`x = 'don''t stop`): the ERROR [0..16] contains child `'` at [4..5]. There's no inner ERROR. So I need the "contains a direct `'` token child" rule. But WAIT — I must be careful: is the `'` child at [4..5] a transpose? No — the preceding char is space (`=` then space then `'`). The transpose guard: check the character before the `'` — space → not transpose → STRIN. ✓

But also — I should be careful NOT to fire STRIN on valid strings. In `x = 'abc';`, the `'` tokens are inside a `string` node, not an ERROR node. My walk is over ERROR nodes only. ✓

Now for the `"` case (DOUQT): `x = "abc;` → ERROR contains child `"` at [4..5]. Fire DOUQT at the `"`. But careful: `s = "\n` → ERROR [0..5] text `s = "`, contains `"` child [4..5]. Fire DOUQT. ✓. And `y = "a\nb\nc";` (valid multi-line) → the `"` tokens are inside a `string` node. The ERROR inside is `(ERROR (UNEXPECTED '\n'))` with text `b\nc` — no `"` child. So no DOUQT. ✓

Hmm, wait — but what about the ERROR node in `y = "a\nb\nc";`? It's `ERROR [7..10]` text `b\nc` — child ERROR [7..10]. No `'` or `"` token child. No STRIN/DOUQT. ✓

Now, one more consideration for DOUQT: what about a `"` that appears inside an ERROR for a DIFFERENT reason, e.g., `x = "abc; y = 2;`? Let me think — the ERROR would be `[0..9]` `x = "abc;` ... then y = 2 parses. Contains `"` child. DOUQT fires at the `"`. ✓.

But here's a concern: could a `"` be a direct child of an ERROR node for a non-string reason? In MATLAB, `"` is only used for strings. So no.

Similarly, could a `'` be a direct child of an ERROR node for a transpose reason? E.g., `x = a' 'b` — weird. Or `x = A' + 'b` hmm. Consider: `x = A' ;` — valid, parses cleanly. What about `x = A' 'b;`? That's `A'` transpose then... a char vector `'b` without close? Actually `'b;` hmm. Let me think about whether a transpose `'` could end up as a direct ERROR child.

The transpose guard handles this: check the char before the `'` token. If it's a letter/digit/`)`/`]`/`}`/`.` (a value that a transpose follows), skip. So `x = A' 'b;` → the first `'` follows `A` → skipped (transpose). Then `'b` — the `'` follows a space... wait, `A' 'b` — the second `'` is preceded by a space → not transpose → STRIN fire at second `'`. That's correct behavior (unterminated char vector `'b`). 

But hold on — what shape does `x = A' 'b;` even parse to? Let me probe that. Also `x = A''` hmm.

Actually, let me simplify. My STRIN detection:

For each ERROR node:
1. If ERROR text starts with `'` → fire STRIN at ERROR start (with preceding-char guard? The preceding char for `x = 'abc;` is space. For `'abc` at file start, no preceding char. For the inner ERROR in `x = ';`, the preceding char of [4..5] is space. All fine. But defensively, apply the guard anyway).
2. If ERROR has a direct child token whose kind is `'` → fire STRIN at that child's start (with transpose guard).

And DOUQT detection:
1. If ERROR has a direct child token whose kind is `"` → fire DOUQT at that child's start.

Wait, I should also consider: are `'` and `"` child node kinds literally `'` and `"`? From the dump: the child kinds are `'` [4..5] and `"` [4..5]. Yes, the kind is the literal character.

Also the inner ERROR child case: `x = 'abc;` has ERROR [4..5] with a child ERROR [4..5] with kind ERROR and text `'`... and that inner ERROR has a child `'` [4..5]. Let me re-check the dump:

```

Hmm, so the outer ERROR [4..5] text `'` has a child ERROR [4..5] text `'` which has NO children shown (the dump didn't show a `'` token child inside it). Wait, the dump shows the inner ERROR [4..5] has no children. So the inner ERROR's text is `'` — it starts with `'` → rule 1 fires. Good.

But also the outer ERROR [4..5] text starts with `'` → rule 1 fires at the same position. So I'd get duplicate STRIN diagnostics at [4..5]. I need dedup via a HashSet of positions. Good, I planned that.

Now for case 2 (`x = 'don''t stop`): ERROR [0..16] contains `'` child [4..5] (kind `'`) and `string_content` [5..16]. Rule 2: direct child `'` → STRIN at [4..5]. ✓ And DOUQT rule: direct child `"` — no. ✓

For DOUQT `x = "abc;`: ERROR [0..9] contains `"` child [4..5]. DOUQT at [4..5]. ✓

Now — the MUST-NOT-fire cases:
- `x = 'abc';` → string node, no ERROR → no STRIN. ✓
- `x = "abc";` → string node, no ERROR → no DOUQT. ✓
- `x = 'it''s ok';` → string node → no STRIN. ✓
- `x = A';` → postfix_operator, no ERROR → no STRIN. ✓
- `x = A.';` → postfix_operator → no STRIN. ✓
- `x = "multi\nline";` → string node with inner ERROR text `line` (no `'`/`"` token child) → no DOUQT. ✓
- `%{ closed %}` → comment → INBLK check: text starts with `%{` AND contains `%}` → no fire. ✓

Let me verify `x = "multi\nline";` inner ERROR: earlier dump for `y = "a\nb\nc";` showed inner ERROR [7..10] text `b\nc` with a nested ERROR [7..10] text `b\nc`. No `'` or `"` child. ✓ 

Now the INBLK check. `%{\nunterminated\n` parses as a single `comment` node. Text starts with `%{`, doesn't contain `%}` → INBLK. ✓. And `%{ comment %}` → contains `%}` → no fire. What about a block comment that spans multiple comment nodes? In MATLAB, `%{ ... %}` is a single comment node per the parse. Let me verify a multi-line block comment: `%{ first line\nsecond line\n%}`. Let me probe. Also nested block comments `%{ %{ %}` ... MATLAB doesn't nest block comments, but the grammar might produce multiple comment nodes. Let me probe.

Also need to check INBLK: what if there's a `%{` inside a regular comment, like `% not a block %{`? Per plan: "a comment node starting with `%{` without `%}` is INBLK". The `%{` must be the START of the comment. Let me verify parse: `x = 1; % hello %{` — is that one comment node text `% hello %{`? Starts with `%` not `%{`, so no fire. Good.

What about `%% section %{`? Also starts with `%`... hmm, `%%` is a section break comment. Text `%% section %{` — does it start with `%{`? No, starts with `%%`. Good.

Edge: `%{` at very start, then EOF without newline: `%{ unterminated` (no trailing newline) → still a comment node. Let me check the parse handles it.

Now — one more thing to verify for DOUQT: the MUST-fire `x = "abc;` where there IS a `"` before EOF but it's... wait no, there's no closing `"`. The ERROR-node approach fires. But what about a case where a `"` opens and there's a closing `"` BUT they're in different ERROR contexts? E.g., `x = "abc"; y = "def` → the second string is unterminated. The ERROR would be `y = "def` containing a `"` child → DOUQT fires at that `"`. ✓

What about `x = "abc` where the closing `"` appears later in a comment: `x = "abc % "` → hmm, `% "` — the `"` is inside a comment. Source-scan would need comment awareness; ERROR-node approach: `x = "abc % "` parses as... ERROR `x = "abc` + comment `% "`. So ERROR contains `"` child → DOUQT fires. Correct! (The `"` in the comment isn't a real close.) ✓

Now, I'm fairly confident about the ERROR-node-based approach. Let me also double check the "preceding char" transpose guard for rule 2 (`'` child token). The plan requires the transpose not-fire tests pass. Since transposes parse as postfix_operator (no ERROR), rule 2 only triggers on `'` tokens that are inside ERROR nodes, which by construction are not successful transposes. The guard is defensive. But wait — could there be a case where a valid transpose IS inside an ERROR node? E.g., `x = A' 'B;`? Let me probe that plus a few more:

- `x = A' 'B;`
- `x = [a b c]' ;` (valid, no error?)
- `x = 5'` — hmm, number transpose is invalid but parses? Let me probe.
- `A''` — double transpose?
- `x = A'` at EOF (no newline).

Let me also probe the multi-comment block comment and `%{` variants for INBLK.

parts.text:
Very interesting! The exact MUST-fire combined source reveals important parse quirks:

**Case 1: `x = 'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched ' before EOL`** (line 1)
Parses as: `assignment [0..50]` containing `ERROR [4..47]` with text `'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched ' befo...`. Inside the ERROR there's a VALID `string` node `[4..39]` text `'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched '` (!!!), followed by comma tokens. 

Wait — this is fascinating. The grammar actually found a closing `'` at position 38 (the `'` in the comment `% STRIN: unmatched '`). So the string `'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched '` — the grammar treats the `%` as part of the string content (since we're inside a char vector), and the `'` at position 38 closes it. That's why it parses as a VALID string! Then the rest (`before EOL`) becomes identifiers and the ERROR is around everything.

So in this combined source, my STRIN detection based on "ERROR text starts with `'`" — the ERROR text is `'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched ' befo...` — IT DOES start with `'`! The ERROR [4..47] text starts with `'`. So rule 1 fires STRIN at [4]. ✓ 

But hold on — is that CORRECT behavior? The line is `x = 'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched ' before EOL`. In real MATLAB, this line: `x = 'abc;` — unterminated char vector? Then `% STRIN: unmatched ' before EOL` — hmm. Actually in real MATLAB, `%` inside a single-quoted char vector IS literal (doesn't start a comment) as long as the char vector is still open. So `'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched '` would be a VALID char vector (the `%` is content), and `before EOL` would be... a syntax error (missing operator). Hmm! So actually the line as written in the plan's test is a valid char vector + garbage! But the plan says it should fire STRIN.

Hmm wait, but the plan's comment says `% STRIN: unmatched ' before EOL` — the `%` here is INTENDED as a comment by the plan author. But MATLAB wouldn't treat it as a comment because the char vector `'abc` is still open! In real MATLAB, `x = 'abc;          % STRIN: unmatched ' before EOL` — the char vector opens at `'` and closes at the NEXT `'` which is the one in "unmatched '" — so the string content is `abc;          % STRIN: unmatched ` and then `before EOL` follows... MATLAB would give an error like "Invalid text character" or unexpected identifier after string. Actually MATLAB would report an error near `before EOL`.

So the plan's MUST-fire test line, when combined with the trailing comment, actually parses as a valid string + error. But STRIN still fires because the ERROR node starts with `'`. The diagnostic points at [4..5] which is the opening `'`. Good enough — the test asserts `has_id(STRIN)`.

Hmm, but wait — I need to be careful. The test for the MUST-fire case: the plan says "fires" tests should use the combined source or individual sources? The plan's Tests section says "fires/not-fires per check (include the transpose not-fire cases for STRIN)." I'll write tests with clean individual sources that reliably fire:

- STRIN fires: `x = 'abc;\n` (clean — ERROR `'` at [4..5]) ✓ verified
- STRIN fires with escaped quote: `x = 'don''t stop\n` → ERROR contains `'` child [4..5] → rule 2 ✓ verified
- STRIN not fires: `x = 'abc';\n`, `x = 'it''s ok';\n`, `x = A';\n`, `x = A.';\n`, `x = A'\n` (no semicolon, EOF), `x = [1 2 3]; y = x';\n` etc.
- DOUQT fires: `x = "abc;\n` → ERROR contains `"` child ✓ verified; `x = "abc\n` (no semicolon); `s = "\n`
- DOUQT not fires: `x = "abc";\n`, `x = "multi\nline";\n` (multi-line valid), `x = "abc % "\n` (hmm — that's a valid string, no fire ✓), `x = "a" + "b";\n`
- INBLK fires: `%{\nunterminated\n` → comment text starts with `%{` no `%}` ✓
- INBLK not fires: `%{\nclosed\n%}\n`, `%{ block %}\n` (single line with close), `x = 1; % hello\n`

Now let me double check the multi-line valid string test won't accidentally fire DOUQT via rule: `y = "a\nb\nc";` → string node with inner ERROR `b\nc` (text `b\nc` — doesn't start with `'`, no `'`/`"` children). ✓ No DOUQT.

Now, what about `x = "multi\nline";` (the plan's MUST-NOT case) — let me make sure. From earlier probe `y = "a\nb\nc";` the inner ERROR text was `b\nc`. So no `"` child. ✓

Wait, I want to double-check `x = "multi\nline";` exactly — the earlier probe of `"x = \"multi\nline\";\n"` showed:
```
(string (string_content) (ERROR (UNEXPECTED 'l')) (string_content))
```
The inner ERROR is `(ERROR (UNEXPECTED 'l'))` — text `line`? Hmm, the earlier first probe showed `(ERROR (UNEXPECTED 'l'))`. The `UNEXPECTED 'l'` — text would be `line`? Let me not worry; it has no `"` child. ✓

**Now the critical case 1 issue:** In the combined MUST-fire source, line 1 `x = 'abc; ... ' before EOL` produces an ERROR node `[4..47]` whose text starts with `'`. Rule 1 fires STRIN. ✓ GOOD.

BUT — I realize there's a subtle problem with rule 1 firing on `x = 'abc' 'def;`:
```
ERROR [10..14] text='def'
  ERROR [10..11] text='''
```
The ERROR text `'def` starts with `'` → rule 1 fires STRIN at [10]. ✓ Correct — `'def` is unterminated.

And `x = 'abc' 'def';` (closed `'def'`):
```
ERROR [4..9] text=''abc''
  string [4..9] text=''abc''
```

fn check_unterminated(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    let mut reported: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();

    if self.is_check_enabled("STRIN") || self.is_check_enabled("DOUQT") {
        self.walk_unterminated_strings(root, source, &mut diagnostics, &mut reported);
    }

    if self.is_check_enabled("INBLK") {
        self.walk_unterminated_comments(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
    }

    diagnostics
}

fn walk_unterminated_strings(&self, node, source, diagnostics, reported) {
    if node.is_error() {
        // STRIN: ERROR node whose text starts with an unmatched single quote.
        let text = &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte().min(source.len())];
        if text.starts_with('\'')
            && text.matches('\'').count() % 2 == 1
            && !reported.contains(&node.start_byte())
            && !Self::is_transpose_position(source, node.start_byte())
        {
            reported.insert(node.start_byte());
            diagnostics.push(Diagnostic { rule_id: "STRIN", ... byte_range: start..start+1, line, column, ... });
        }

        // Direct quote tokens inside the ERROR node (STRIN/DOUQT).
        let mut cursor = node.walk();
        for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
            if child.kind() == "'" {
                let pos = child.start_byte();
                if !reported.contains(&pos) && !Self::is_transpose_position(source, pos) {
                    reported.insert(pos);
                    diagnostics.push(STRIN at pos);
                }
            } else if child.kind() == "\"" {
                let pos = child.start_byte();
                if !reported.contains(&pos) {
                    reported.insert(pos);
                    diagnostics.push(DOUQT at pos);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // recurse
    let mut cursor = node.walk();
    for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
        self.walk_unterminated_strings(child, source, diagnostics, reported);
    }
}

**Default severity:** Error
**Auto-fix:** No
**Category:** Syntax Errors
**Can be disabled:** Yes

## What this rule does

Flags assignments where the left side is a multi-output list that contains a row separator (`;`). A multi-output assignment target must be a single row — each output separated by a comma:

```matlab
[a;b] = f();    % ';' creates a second row — invalid LHS
```

This is a sub-check of the `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` rule. It triggers on `assignment` nodes whose `left` field is a `multioutput_variable` whose text contains a `;`.

## Why this matters

- **Broken code**: `[a;b] = f()` is not valid MATLAB — the LHS of an assignment must be a single row, so the code fails to run
- **Intent**: The author almost certainly meant `[a, b] = f()` (two outputs) or `[a; b]` on the right side (a matrix literal); the row separator on the LHS is a typo
- **Diagnosis**: The Code Analyzer message ("The left side of an assignment cannot have multiple rows") identifies the exact problem instead of a generic parse error

## Examples

### Correct

```matlab
[a, b] = f();     % comma-separated multi-output LHS
x = f();          % single output
[a, b] = deal(1, 2);
```

### Incorrect

```matlab
[a;b] = f();      % ';' creates multiple rows on the LHS
[a; b] = f();     % same problem, with whitespace
```

### Fixed

```matlab
[a, b] = f();     % comma-separated multi-output LHS
```

## Configuration

As a sub-check of the `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE`, disable it via the engine's `disabled_checks` list:

```toml title=".mlt.toml"
[lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]
severity = "error"
disabled_checks = ["LHROW"]
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `severity` | string | `"error"` | Severity level (`"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`, `"off"`) |
| `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Sub-check IDs to disable within `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` (add `"LHROW"` to disable this check) |

## Automatic fixes

None. Replacing `;` with `,` is a plausible fix, but mlt does not apply it automatically because the author's intent (two outputs vs. a matrix) cannot be determined with certainty.

## Target node types

This rule triggers on the following tree-sitter node types:

- `assignment` — where the `left` field is a `multioutput_variable` containing a `;`

## Related rules

- `UNSET` — invalid use of an operator on the left side of an assignment
- `NOLHS` — assignment with an empty left side

# STRIN - Unterminated Quoted Character Vector

**Default severity:** Error
**Auto-fix:** No
**Category:** Syntax Errors
**Can be disabled:** Yes

## What this rule does

Flags a single-quoted character vector (`'abc'`) that is not terminated before the end of the line. In MATLAB, a character vector delimited by single quotes must be closed with a second `'` on the same line — it cannot span lines.

This is a sub-check of the `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` rule. It triggers on `ERROR` nodes that start with an unmatched `'` (an opening quote with no closing quote before end-of-line) or that contain a stray `'` token.

## Why this matters

- **Broken code**: An unterminated character vector is a syntax error — the code fails to parse and will not run
- **Diagnosis**: The Code Analyzer message ("A quoted character vector is unterminated") identifies the exact problem instead of a generic parse error
- **Ambiguity**: Without this check, an unmatched `'` is easy to miss among transpose operators (`A'`), which is why the rule only fires when the quote is not in transpose position

## Examples

### Correct

```matlab
x = 'abc';          % closed on the same line
x = 'it''s ok';     % doubled '' is an escaped quote
x = A';             % ' is the transpose operator, not a string
x = A.';            % element-wise transpose
```

### Incorrect

```matlab
x = 'abc;           % opening ' never closed before end of line
x = 'don''t stop    % escaped quote still needs a closing '
```

### Fixed

```matlab
x = 'abc';
x = 'don''t stop';
```

## Configuration

As a sub-check of the `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE`, disable it via the engine's `disabled_checks` list:

```toml title=".mlt.toml"
[lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]
severity = "error"
disabled_checks = ["STRIN"]
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `severity` | string | `"error"` | Severity level (`"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`, `"off"`) |
| `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Sub-check IDs to disable within `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` (add `"STRIN"` to disable this check) |

## Automatic fixes

None. mlt cannot know where the closing quote was intended to go.

## Target node types

This rule triggers on the following tree-sitter node types:

- `ERROR` — nodes starting with an unmatched `'`, or containing a stray `'` token in a non-transpose position

A `'` is treated as the transpose operator (and ignored) when the character before it is a letter, digit, `)`, `]`, `}`, or `.`. Valid transposes parse as `postfix_operator` nodes and never trigger this rule.

## Related rules

- `DOUQT` — unterminated double-quoted string
- `INBLK` — unterminated block comment
